lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: This is unbelievable.
lines.translation: 这太令人难以置信了。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Unlike any video game I’ve ever played before, it’s so boring, yet so relaxing at the same time.
lines.translation: 它和我以前玩过的任何电子游戏都不同，虽然很无聊，但同时又让人感到非常放松。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: How did you hear about this driving simulator?
lines.translation: 你是怎么听说这个驾驶模拟器的？

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: My brother introduced it to me last year.
lines.translation: 我哥哥去年把它介绍给我的。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I was surprised to find how educational and realistic it was.
lines.translation: 我很惊讶地发现它竟然如此具有教育意义且如此逼真。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: It’s called Euro Truck Simulator, but they have other versions as well for America and so on.
lines.translation: 它叫《欧洲卡车模拟》，但他们也有美洲等其他版本的衍生作品。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I was really drawn to the scenery.
lines.translation: 我真的被里面的风景吸引了。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: The routes go through parts of the country you don’t normally see as a tourist.
lines.translation: 这些路线会穿过一些你作为游客平时根本见不到的国家区域。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Yeah, I can see that.
lines.translation: 是的，我看得出来。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: It seems so simple, just transporting cargo from point A to point B, driving from one city to another.
lines.translation: 它看起来如此简单，只是把货物从A点运到B点，从一个城市开到另一个城市。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: But I really appreciate all the details that go into the game.
lines.translation: 但我真的很赞赏这款游戏中所融入的所有细节。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: It’s even given me a new appreciation for the logistics industry and traffic on the road.
lines.translation: 它甚至让我对物流行业和道路交通有了新的认识和理解。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I completely agree.
lines.translation: 我完全同意。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: My brother also introduced me to some videos of someone that streams their game online.
lines.translation: 我哥哥还给我推荐了一些人在网上直播玩这款游戏的视频。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: It was fascinating to watch, really.
lines.translation: 看那个真的非常有意思。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: This guy drove very carefully, obeyed all the road signs and traffic rules—such a contrast to most violent games.
lines.translation: 那个人开车非常小心，遵守所有的路标和交通规则——这与大多数暴力游戏形成了鲜明的对比。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Honestly, playing has inspired me to look into the industry more.
lines.translation: 说实话，玩这个游戏激发了我去进一步了解这个行业的兴趣。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: I’ve read articles about how self-driving trucks may soon be available and could greatly impact cargo logistics.
lines.translation: 我读过一些文章，说自动驾驶卡车可能很快就会问世，并可能对货物物流产生巨大影响。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Considering all that goes into driving these larger vehicles, it’s amazing that we could soon have that kind of technology.
lines.translation: 考虑到驾驶这些大型车辆所需的各种复杂操作，我们很快就能拥有这种技术真是太不可思议了。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Ha.
lines.translation: 哈。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I’ve gone one step further.
lines.translation: 我做得更彻底。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I registered to take a safe driving course to improve my real-life driving skills.
lines.translation: 我报名参加了一个安全驾驶课程，以提高我现实生活中的驾驶技术。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: In a way, I feel like I have a head start compared to other students in the class.
lines.translation: 在某种程度上，我觉得和班上的其他学生相比，我已经占了先机。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Playing this video game has given me some maneuvering practices already.
lines.translation: 玩这个电子游戏已经让我进行了一些车辆操控方面的练习。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: I’m not sure how accurate the video game is compared to real-life situations.
lines.translation: 我不确定这款电子游戏与现实生活中的情况相比有多准确。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: But if it results in more drivers looking both ways before entering an intersection, I’d say that’s a postive outcome.
lines.translation: 但如果它能让更多的司机在进入交叉路口前先看两边，我会说那是一个积极的结果。

lines.speaker: Q1.
lines.text: What are the speakers mainly talking about?
lines.translation: 说话者主要在谈论什么？

lines.speaker: Q2.
lines.text: What does the man say about the driving simulator?
lines.translation: 关于这个驾驶模拟器，这位男士说了什么？

lines.speaker: Q3.
lines.text: What does the woman say she really appreciates?
lines.translation: 这位女士说她真正赞赏的是什么？

lines.speaker: Q4.
lines.text: What outcome does the woman expect from the driving simulator?
lines.translation: 这位女士期望从驾驶模拟器中得到什么结果？

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: How do you like being self-employed?
lines.translation: 你觉得自主创业（自由职业）怎么样？

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: There are obvious benefits, though I don’t seem to have the freedom I anticipated as I just don’t seem able to decline work offers.
lines.translation: 好处是显而易见的，尽管我似乎并没有得到预期的自由，因为我好像根本无法拒绝别人提供的工作机会。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: And working alone, there have been times when I’ve found that money alone provides insufficient motivation.
lines.translation: 而且独自工作，有时候我会发现单靠金钱并不能提供足够的动力。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Have you experienced the same since you began working for yourself?
lines.translation: 自从你开始为自己工作以来，你也有过同样的经历吗？

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Sometimes, yes.
lines.translation: 有时是的。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Unlike the rest of the workforce who have managers to prompt motivation whenever they’re feeling lazy or bored, we self-employed workers perform our jobs without a manager to lift our spirits.
lines.translation: 其他上班族在感到懒散或无聊时会有经理来督促激励，而我们这些自主创业的人在做工作时，没有经理来提振我们的精神。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: There’s no one around to offer praise or initiate collaboration, no one to make greater use of our interests and talents.
lines.translation: 身边没有人给予赞赏或发起合作，也没有人能更好地利用我们的兴趣和才能。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: That’s a fact.
lines.translation: 这确实是事实。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care, of course.
lines.translation: 当然，并不是每个经理都有这样的意识和关怀。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: And certainly not all managers have a clue how to motivate people.
lines.translation: 而且肯定不是所有经理都懂得如何去激励员工。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Still, having a manager nearby at least indicates there’s an opportunity they'll be decent enough to look out for you when your energy and focus begin to deplete.
lines.translation: 尽管如此，身边有个经理至少意味着，当你的精力和注意力开始消耗殆尽时，他们有可能还算通情达理地来关照你。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: The motivator I value most is autonomy.
lines.translation: 我最看重的动力源泉是自主权。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: I’ve learned not to sacrifice my prized autonomy by working all hours of the day and by saying yes to every client request.
lines.translation: 我已经学会了不要通过没日没夜地工作以及对客户的每个要求都说“好”，来牺牲我所珍视的自主权。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Yes.
lines.translation: 是的。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I need to remind myself that I selected this lifestyle for the independence.
lines.translation: 我需要提醒自己，我选择这种生活方式是为了独立。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I don’t miss aspects of permanent full-time employment I disliked, such as the office politics, job insecurity, inflexible hours and so on.
lines.translation: 我一点也不怀念全职固定工作中那些我讨厌的方面，比如办公室政治、缺乏工作安全感、僵化的时间安排等等。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I wouldn’t mind a bit more in the form of praise though, praise which is on the record.
lines.translation: 不过，我倒不介意多得到一些形式上的赞赏，那种有记录在案的赞赏。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: That’ll come with time.
lines.translation: 那会随着时间推移而到来的。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Relatedness is inevitably cultivated via human interaction.
lines.translation: 归属感（人际联系）必然是在人际互动中培养出来的。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Engaging with clients, getting written testimony and recommendations, staying in contact with clients afterwards, these are things you’ll find will come in due course and provide you with motivation.
lines.translation: 与客户接洽、获得书面证明和推荐信、事后与客户保持联系，你会发现这些事情自会水到渠成，并为你提供动力。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: You’re right.
lines.translation: 你说得对。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: That’s an area I do need to put some more effort into—building closer relationships with those who engage my services and skills.
lines.translation: 这确实是我需要投入更多精力的地方——与那些使用我的服务和技能的人建立更紧密的联系。

lines.speaker: Q5.
lines.text: What does the man say about his life of being self-employed?
lines.translation: 关于自主创业的生活，这位男士说了什么？

lines.speaker: Q6.
lines.text: What does the man say about managers?
lines.translation: 关于经理，这位男士说了什么？

lines.speaker: Q7.
lines.text: What do both speakers value most about self-employment?
lines.translation: 两位说话者最看重自主创业的什么？

lines.speaker: Q8.
lines.text: On what point does the man agree with the woman?
lines.translation: 在哪个观点上，这位男士同意这位女士的看法？

lines.text: Weather is a constant force in our lives, but there is little marketing research on how it affects businesses.
lines.translation: 天气是我们生活中一种恒定的力量，但关于它如何影响商业的营销研究却很少。

lines.text: Now, a new study reveals how sunny and snowy conditions influence consumer behavior.
lines.translation: 现在，一项新研究揭示了晴天和下雪天气是如何影响消费者行为的。

lines.text: Those weather conditions trigger consumers to mentally visualize using products associated with the respective weather.
lines.translation: 这些天气条件会触发消费者在脑海中想象使用与相应天气相关的产品。

lines.text: This leads to consumers placing a higher value on those products.
lines.translation: 这导致消费者对这些产品赋予更高的价值。

lines.text: That is, they’re willing to pay more money for them.
lines.translation: 也就是说，他们愿意为此支付更多的钱。

lines.text: But the correlation is only found with products related to being outside.
lines.translation: 但这种相关性仅在与户外活动相关的产品中被发现。

lines.text: How does this work?
lines.translation: 这是如何起作用的呢？

lines.text: Researchers give the example of a beach towel.
lines.translation: 研究人员以沙滩巾为例。

lines.text: On a sunny day, consumers who see that product are not just looking at the towel itself, they are likely imagining themselves lying on the towel in the sun.
lines.translation: 在晴天，看到该产品的消费者不仅仅是在看浴巾本身，他们很可能在想象自己躺在阳光下的浴巾上。

lines.text: This mental picture of using the towel increases the value of the product in the consumers’ mind.
lines.translation: 这种使用浴巾的脑海画面提升了该产品在消费者心中的价值。

lines.text: Researchers put forward the following hypothesis to explain their findings.
lines.translation: 研究人员提出了以下假设来解释他们的发现。

lines.text: They think the mental picture works in sunshine and snow because these weather conditions have a positive association with outside activities.
lines.translation: 他们认为脑海画面在晴天和下雪时起作用，是因为这些天气条件与户外活动有积极的关联。

lines.text: The effect is not seen with rainy weather.
lines.translation: 这种效应在下雨天则看不到。

lines.text: Researchers assert this is because there aren’t many activities that are enabled by rain.
lines.translation: 研究人员断言，这是因为没有多少活动是由下雨促成的。

lines.text: Most products associated with rain, like umbrellas, are only used for protection from the weather, and not for any activities.
lines.translation: 大多数与雨相关的产品（如雨伞）仅用于防雨，而不是为了进行任何活动。

lines.text: Researchers believe that companies that sell a wide array of products online can benefit most from the insights this study provides.
lines.translation: 研究人员认为，在网上销售种类繁多产品的公司能从这项研究提供的见解中获益最多。

lines.text: Online sellers often use complex mathematical formulas to determine what products to feature and how to price these products.
lines.translation: 在线卖家经常使用复杂的数学公式来决定展示哪些产品以及如何为这些产品定价。

lines.text: Incorporating more data about weather would allow them to make better decisions.
lines.translation: 纳入更多关于天气的数据将使他们能够做出更好的决策。

lines.text: This could bolster sales.
lines.translation: 这可以刺激销售。

lines.speaker: Q9.
lines.text: What do we learn about the findings of the new study?
lines.translation: 关于这项新研究的发现，我们了解到了什么？

lines.speaker: Q10.
lines.text: What does the passage say may increase the value of products for consumers?
lines.translation: 文章说可能是什么增加了产品对消费者的价值？

lines.speaker: Q11.
lines.text: How can the findings of the new study benefit online sellers according to the researchers?
lines.translation: 根据研究人员的说法，这项新研究的发现如何能让在线卖家受益？

lines.text: Setting the office air-conditioning at about 22℃ has become standard practice across the world.
lines.translation: 将办公室空调设定在22℃左右已成为世界各地的标准做法。

lines.text: Numerous guidebooks across the world on heating, ventilation and air-conditioning claim office performance peaks at 22 degrees.
lines.translation: 全球许多关于供暖、通风和空调的指导手册都声称，办公室的工作效率在22度时达到峰值。

lines.text: Many people indeed find relief from soaring summer temperatures in air-conditioned offices.
lines.translation: 在空调办公室里，许多人确实从酷暑的高温中得到了解脱。

lines.text: But recent studies have challenged the accepted wisdom that a cool office is more productive.
lines.translation: 但最近的研究挑战了“凉爽的办公室效率更高”这一普遍公认的观点。

lines.text: The reality is more complex.
lines.translation: 现实情况更为复杂。

lines.text: Researchers conducted a review of all studies relating to air-conditioning and productivity.
lines.translation: 研究人员对所有关于空调与生产力（效率）相关的研究进行了系统审查。

lines.text: They found that 22 degrees was probably a little chilly, even at the height of summer.
lines.translation: 他们发现，即使在盛夏，22度可能也有点太凉了。

lines.text: For a person dressed in typical summer clothing, an optimal range would be between 23 and 26 degrees.
lines.translation: 对于一个穿着典型夏季服装的人来说，最适宜的温度范围应该在23到26度之间。

lines.text: And people can even tolerate temperatures beyond this comfort zone as long as they can adjust their clothing and expectations.
lines.translation: 而且只要人们能够调整自己的衣着和预期心理，他们甚至可以忍受超出这个舒适区的温度。

lines.text: In fact, even on very hot days, it makes sense to turn the air-conditioning up.
lines.translation: 事实上，即使在非常炎热的日子里，将空调调高几度（减少冷气）也是明智的。

lines.text: People often chase just one optimum temperature, and this is understandable when people feel hot.
lines.translation: 人们常常只追求一个最理想的温度，这在人们感到炎热时是可以理解的。

lines.text: But there is a range of at least three to four degrees which does not have any adverse impact.
lines.translation: 但是存在着至少有三到四度波动的范围，在这个范围内是不会产生任何负面影响的。

lines.text: Another issue related to this is that people can become psychologically dependent on air conditioning.
lines.translation: 与此相关的另一个问题是，人们可能会对空调产生心理依赖。

lines.text: If they’re used to the environment which is air-conditioned, they tend to prefer lower temperatures.
lines.translation: 如果他们习惯了有空调的环境，他们往往会更倾向于更低的温度。

lines.text: But the studies found that almost all humans became accustomed to the new temperature.
lines.translation: 但研究发现，几乎所有人都能习惯新的温度。

lines.text: It was only at the extreme ends of the temperature range where people’s productivity suffered.
lines.translation: 只有在温度范围的极端两端，人们的生产效率才会受到损害。

lines.text: This range was above 26 degrees and below 19 degrees.
lines.translation: 这个范围是指26度以上和19度以下。

lines.speaker: Q12.
lines.text: What is the accepted wisdom concerning the office environment?
lines.translation: 关于办公室环境，普遍公认的观点是什么？

lines.speaker: Q13.
lines.text: What did researchers find from their review of all studies relating to air-conditioning and productivity?
lines.translation: 研究人员从他们对所有关于空调与生产力相关研究的审查中发现了什么？

lines.speaker: Q14.
lines.text: What do we learn about using a little less air-conditioning during hot weather?
lines.translation: 关于在炎热天气里少用一点空调（调高温度），我们了解到了什么？

lines.speaker: Q15.
lines.text: What happens when people are used to an air-conditioned environment?
lines.translation: 当人们习惯了空调环境后会发生什么？

lines.text: Psychology research has tended to portray solitude as a negative experience.
lines.translation: 心理学研究往往将独处描绘成一种消极的体验。

lines.text: Studies conducted in the 1970s and 1990s suggested that people felt less happy when alone as compared to being with others.
lines.translation: 在20世纪70年代和90年代进行的研究表明，与和他人在一起相比，人们在独自一人时感到不那么快乐。

lines.text: However, a new paper shows an alternative view of solitude, one in which solitude can be positive.
lines.translation: 然而，一篇新论文展示了对独处的另一种看法，即独处也可以是积极的。

lines.text: Let's start by looking at the earlier research.
lines.translation: 让我们首先来看一下早期的研究。

lines.text: It had a couple of shortcomings.
lines.translation: 它有几个缺点。

lines.text: First, it measured emotion on a scale from positive to negative, overlooking the possibility that our positive and negative emotions can fluctuate independently.
lines.translation: 第一，它在从积极到消极的单一维度上衡量情绪，忽略了我们的积极情绪和消极情绪可以独立波动的可能性。

lines.text: Also, it categorized emotions as simply positive or negative.
lines.translation: 此外，它把情绪简单地归类为积极或消极。

lines.text: It didn’t consider that emotions arouse us to different degrees, and that both positive and negative emotions can arouse us a lot or a little.
lines.translation: 它没有考虑到情绪会激发我们到不同的程度，而且积极和消极的情绪都可以强烈地或轻微地激发我们。

lines.text: That is, whether positive or negative, emotions can be either high-arousal or low-arousal.
lines.translation: 也就是说，无论积极还是消极，情绪都可以是高唤醒（高强度）或低唤醒（低强度）的。

lines.text: High-arousal emotions include excitement on the positive side or anger on the negative side, while low-arousal ones include feeling calm on the positive side or lonely on the negative.
lines.translation: 高唤醒情绪包括积极一面的兴奋或消极一面的愤怒；而低唤醒情绪包括积极一面的平静或消极一面的孤独。

lines.text: This new research attempted to overcome these shortcomings.
lines.translation: 这项新研究试图克服这些缺点。

lines.text: Researchers began with a simple study.
lines.translation: 研究人员从一项简单的研究开始。

lines.text: They asked participants to spend 15 minutes sitting alone without engaging in any activity, and measured how this solitude influences their emotional state.
lines.translation: 他们要求参与者独自静坐15分钟，不进行任何活动，并测量这种独处如何影响他们的情绪状态。

lines.text: This experiment specifically aimed to determine the effect of solitude on high-arousal emotions.
lines.translation: 这个实验特别旨在确定独处对高唤醒情绪的影响。

lines.text: It looked at positive emotions such as being excited or interested and negative emotions including being scared or distressed.
lines.translation: 它观察了诸如兴奋或感兴趣等积极情绪，以及包括害怕或痛苦在内的消极情绪。

lines.text: The results were clear.
lines.translation: 结果非常明了。

lines.text: After 15 minutes of solitude, the participants showed reductions in both types of emotion.
lines.translation: 在独处15分钟后，参与者的这两种情绪都有所减弱。

lines.text: A second study measured the effects of solitude on low-arousal emotions.
lines.translation: 第二项研究测量了独处对低唤醒情绪的影响。

lines.text: These included both positive and negative emotions, such as feeling calm, relaxed, sad or lonely.
lines.translation: 这些包括积极和消极的情情绪，例如感到平静、放松、悲伤或孤独。

lines.text: That experiment found that all of these emotions were increased by time alone.
lines.translation: 该实验发现，所有这些情绪都会因为独自一人呆着而增强。

lines.text: Thus it seems past depictions of solitude were wrong.
lines.translation: 因此，过去对独处的描绘似乎是错误的。

lines.text: It doesn’t have a simple emotional effect that can be characterized as good or bad.
lines.translation: 它并没有一个可以被简单定性为好或坏的情绪效应。

lines.text: Rather, it changes the intensity of our inner experience.
lines.translation: 更确切地说，它改变了我们内心体验的强度。

lines.text: It amplifies quieter emotions, but it diminishes the intensity of stronger feelings.
lines.translation: 它放大了较平静的情绪，但减弱了较强烈情感的强度。

lines.text: It’s worth clarifying that these findings relate to relatively brief periods of solitude.
lines.translation: 需要澄清的是，这些发现与相对较短时间的独处有关。

lines.text: This is distinct from prolonged loneliness.
lines.translation: 这与长期的孤独是截然不同的。

lines.text: Research has demonstrated that the latter is correlated with an assortment of negative physical and psychological effects.
lines.translation: 研究已经表明，后者与各种负面的生理和心理效应相关。

lines.text: How can people benefit from being alone?
lines.translation: 人们如何能从独处中获益？

lines.text: The findings here suggest that people can use solitude to regulate their emotions.
lines.translation: 这里的发现表明，人们可以利用独处来调节自己的情绪。

lines.text: Solitude can help us become quiet after excitement, calm after an angry episode, or simply feel at peace.
lines.translation: 独处可以帮助我们在兴奋之后回归安静，在愤怒发作后冷静下来，或者仅仅是感到内心平和。

lines.speaker: Q16.
lines.text: What is one of the criticisms directed at the early research on solitude?
lines.translation: 针对早期关于独处的研究，其中一个批评是什么？

lines.speaker: Q17.
lines.text: What do we learn about the results of the new research?
lines.translation: 关于这项新研究的结果，我们了解到了什么？

lines.speaker: Q18.
lines.text: What did the second experiment in the new research find about solitude?
lines.translation: 新研究中的第二个实验发现了关于独处的什么结论？

lines.text: In 1984, the World Chess Championship was called off abruptly, due to the withered frame of a player who was competing for the title.
lines.translation: 1984年，世界国际象棋锦标赛突然宣告取消，原因是一位正在争夺冠军的选手身体极度消瘦虚弱。

lines.text: He wasn’t alone in experiencing the extreme physical effects of the game.
lines.translation: 在承受这款游戏带来的极端生理影响方面，他并不是唯一的个例。

lines.text: Elite players can reportedly burn up to an absurd 6,000 calories in one day.
lines.translation: 据报道，顶尖棋手在一天内可以消耗掉高达荒谬的6000卡路里。

lines.text: Does that mean that thinking harder is a simple route to losing weight?
lines.translation: 这是否意味着更用力地去思考是减肥的一条捷径？

lines.text: Well, when the body is at rest, we know that the brain uses up a startling 20% to 25% of the body’s overall energy.
lines.translation: 好吧，我们知道当身体处于休息状态时，大脑会消耗掉人体总能量的20%到25%，这个比例令人吃惊。

lines.text: This level of utilization actually makes the brain the most energy-expensive organ in the body, and yet it makes up only 2% of the body’s weight overall.
lines.translation: 这种利用水平实际上使大脑成为体内最耗能的器官，然而它却仅占人体总重量的2%。

lines.text: So the more we put this organ to work, the more calories we’ll burn?
lines.translation: 那么，我们越让这个器官工作，燃烧的卡路里就越多吗？

lines.text: Technically, the answer is yes, for cognitively difficult tasks.
lines.translation: 从技术上讲，对于认知难度大的任务，答案是肯定的。

lines.text: What counts as a “difficult” mental task varies between individuals.
lines.translation: 什么算是“困难”的心理任务因人而异。

lines.text: But generally, it could be described as something that the brain cannot solve easily using previously learned routines, or tasks that change the conditions continuously.
lines.translation: 但总的来说，它可以被描述为大脑无法利用先前学到的常规轻松解决的事情，或者是条件不断发生变化的任务。

lines.text: However, deep thinking will not burn off the calories gained from eating a sugary snack.
lines.translation: 然而，深度思考并不能消耗掉吃含糖零食所摄入的卡路里。

lines.text: Because in relation to the brain’s huge overall energy usage, which is devoted to a multitude of tasks, the energy required just to think harder is actually comparatively tiny.
lines.translation: 因为相对于大脑用于处理众多任务的巨大总能量消耗而言，仅仅为了更努力思考所需的能量实际上是微不足道的。

lines.text: We are unconscious of most of what uses up the brain’s energy.
lines.translation: 我们对消耗大脑大部分能量的活动是毫无意识的。

lines.text: A lot of that activity is unrelated to conscious activities like learning how to sing or play the guitar.
lines.translation: 许多此类活动与学唱歌或弹吉他等有意识的活动无关。

lines.text: The brain is able to allocate blood (and thus energy) to particular regions that are being active at that point.
lines.translation: 大脑能够将血液（也就是能量）分配给当时正处于活跃状态的特定区域。

lines.text: But the overall energy availability in the brain is thought to be constant.
lines.translation: 但大脑中的整体可用能量被认为是恒定的。

lines.text: So, while there might be significant increases in energy use at localized regions of the brain when we perform difficult cognitive tasks, when it comes to the whole brain’s energy budget overall, these activities don’t significantly alter it.
lines.translation: 因此，虽然当我们执行困难的认知任务时，大脑局部区域的能量消耗可能会显著增加，但就整个大脑的总能量预算而言，这些活动并不会显著改变它。

lines.text: So why did the chess champion grow too skinny to compete in his chess competition?
lines.translation: 那么，为什么这位象棋冠军会变得太瘦而无法参加他的象棋比赛呢？

lines.text: The general consensus is that it mostly comes down to stress and reduced food consumption, not mental exhaustion.
lines.translation: 普遍的共识是，这主要归因于压力和进食量减少，而不是精神衰竭。

lines.text: Keeping your body pumped up for action for long periods of time is very energy demanding.
lines.translation: 让身体长时间保持高度集中的临战状态是非常消耗能量的。

lines.text: If you can’t eat as often or as much as you can or would normally—then you might lose weight.
lines.translation: 如果你不能像平时那样经常或吃那么多东西——那么你可能就会体重减轻。

lines.speaker: Q19.
lines.text: What do we learn about the brain when the body is at rest?
lines.translation: 当身体处于休息状态时，我们对大脑有了什么了解？

lines.speaker: Q20.
lines.text: What does the speaker say about the consumption of the brain’s energy?
lines.translation: 发言者关于大脑能量的消耗说了什么？

lines.speaker: Q21.
lines.text: What do we learn about the overall energy availability in the brain?
lines.translation: 关于大脑的整体可用能量，我们了解到了什么？

lines.text: “Tell me about yourself” may seem like an easy job interview question, but the open-ended nature of this question often leaves job seekers at a loss where to start.
lines.translation: “谈谈你自己吧”似乎是一个简单的求职面试问题，但这个问题开放式的性质往往让求职者不知从何说起。

lines.text: This common question is actually a critical test of a job candidate’s communication skills.
lines.translation: 这个常见的问题实际上是对求职者沟通能力的一项关键测试。

lines.text: So it’s important not to give an unprepared response or mess it up.
lines.translation: 因此，重要的是不要给出一个毫无准备的回答，或者把事情搞砸。

lines.text: “Tell me about yourself” is often the first question professional career coaches prepare people for when they give interview guidance.
lines.translation: 当专业的职业导师提供面试指导时，“谈谈你自己吧”往往是他们让求职者准备第一个问题。

lines.text: It’s the opportunity for the candidate to take control of the narrative and tell their story in a way that really matters to their audience.
lines.translation: 这是求职者掌控话语权、并以一种对听众（面试官）真正重要的方式讲述自己故事的机会。

lines.text: It takes hard work and extensive preparation to answer this question well.
lines.translation: 要回答好这个问题需要付出努力和广泛的准备。

lines.text: When a person goes to a job interview, their interviewer has presumably read their résumé, so they don’t need to repeat the information.
lines.translation: 当一个人去参加求职面试时，他们的面试官想必已经看过了他们的简历，所以他们不需要重复这些信息。

lines.text: But that’s what most people will do, as it’s their instinct to recite things that are already on their résumé.
lines.translation: 但大多数人都会这样做，因为背诵简历上已经有的内容是他们的本能。

lines.text: It’s important for job seekers to do their homework on two crucial aspects.
lines.translation: 求职者在两个关键方面做好功课非常重要。

lines.text: First, they are not just telling someone a fact about themselves.
lines.translation: 第一，他们不仅仅是在向某人陈述一个关于他们自己的事实。

lines.text: They’re telling a story.
lines.translation: 他们是在讲一个故事。

lines.text: And stories take work to create.
lines.translation: 而故事是需要花心思去创作的。

lines.text: Coming up with a good story means getting reflective about what made their career accomplishments—something they’re proud of, and what strengths those accomplishments highlight.
lines.translation: 想出一个好故事意味着要反思是什么铸就了他们的职业成就——那些让他们引以为豪的事情，以及这些成就凸显了哪些优势。

lines.text: Candidates shouldn’t pick a broad general strength to elaborate on, such as “I’m smart.
lines.translation: 应聘者不应该选择一个宽泛、笼统的优点来阐述，比如“我很聪明”。

lines.text: I work hard and I get things done.
lines.translation: “我很努力，而且能把事情办好。”

lines.text: ” To come up with multiple career accomplishments or examples for different interview questions, job seekers should talk with others, especially people who know them, partners, friends or co-workers who will bring up different stories than the ones they remember.
lines.translation: 为了针对不同的面试问题想出多个职业成就或例子，求职者应该与他人交谈，尤其是了解他们的人、伴侣、朋友或同事，他们会提及一些与求职者自己记忆中不同的故事。

lines.text: Secondly, candidates should know what's at stake for the company with this job opening.
lines.translation: 其次，应聘者应该了解这个职位空缺对公司的利害关系所在。

lines.text: What they really are asking you is “tell me why you are going to help me.
lines.translation: 他们真正想问你的是：“告诉我，你将如何帮助我。”

lines.text: ” If the person is a prepared candidate, they should have already figured out those things.
lines.translation: 如果这个人是一个有准备的应聘者，他们应该已经弄清楚了这些事情。

lines.text: They’ve read the job description and researched the company on the Internet.
lines.translation: 他们已经阅读了职位说明，并在互联网上对该公司进行了研究。

lines.text: What job applicants ought to be looking for is what the company is up to, what they are trying to accomplish and what is preventing them from accomplishing those things.
lines.translation: 求职者应该寻找的是这家公司目前在做什么、他们试图实现什么目标，以及是什么在阻碍他们实现这些目标。

lines.text: How long should it take to answer?
lines.translation: 回答应该花多长时间？

lines.text: Around a minute.
lines.translation: 一分钟左右。

lines.text: That’s about right for most people’s attention spans.
lines.translation: 这正符合大多数人的注意力持续时间。

lines.text: Under a minute could seem rushed, while over two minutes will start to feel more like a speech.
lines.translation: 少于一分钟可能显得太仓促，而超过两分钟就会开始感觉更像是在做演讲。

lines.text: But the length of the answer is not an exact science, and candidates need to keep their career story focused and tailored to their audience.
lines.translation: 但回答的长度并不是一门精确的科学，应聘者需要让他们的职业故事保持焦点，并因人制宜地迎合听众。

lines.speaker: Q22.
lines.text: What does the speaker say about the job interview question “tell me about yourself”?
lines.translation: 发言人关于求职面试问题“谈谈你自己”说了什么？

lines.speaker: Q23.
lines.text: What will most people do when they come to a job interview?
lines.translation: 大多数人在参加求职面试时会怎么做？

lines.speaker: Q24.
lines.text: Why should job seekers talk with partners, friends and co-workers?
lines.translation: 为什么求职者应该与伴侣、朋友和同事交谈？

lines.speaker: Q25.
lines.text: What other important preparations should job seekers make before an interview?
lines.translation: 求职者在面试前还应该做哪些重要的准备工作？
